spec.title: Add change_email to shop.users (plus Database update support)
spec.goal: Users currently have no way to change their email address after registration. Add a `change_email(db, user_id, new_email)` service function in `shop/users.py` that normalises the new email to lowercase, rejects emails already taken by another user, and fails cleanly for unknown user ids. The in-memory `Database` needs a lookup-by-id and a row update primitive to support this.
constraints: Reuse existing exception types where they already exist (`UserNotFound`); new exceptions live alongside it in `shop/users.py`
acceptance_criteria: `Database` gains the methods needed to look a row up by id and to update fields on an existing row, usable independently of the users module
spec.technical_notes:
In `shop/db.py`, add two small methods to `Database`:
- `get(table, row_id) -> dict | None` — implement via the existing `find_one(table, id=row_id)` to avoid duplicating the scan logic.
- `update(table, row_id, values) -> bool` — locate the row by id and merge `values` into it in place (mutating the dict already in `self.tables`), returning whether a row was updated. Never allow `id` to be overwritten.

In `shop/users.py`:
- Add `class EmailTaken(Exception): pass` next to `UserNotFound`.
- `change_email(db, user_id, new_email)`: normalise with `new_email.lower()`; fetch the current row with `db.get("users", user_id)` and raise `UserNotFound(user_id)` if it is `None`; check for a conflict with `db.find_one("users", email=normalised)` and raise `EmailTaken(normalised)` only if the found row's `id` differs from `user_id`; then `db.update("users", user_id, {"email": normalised})` and return `User(row["id"], normalised, row["password_hash"])`.
- Order matters: unknown-id check before the taken-email check, so a bogus id with a taken email raises `UserNotFound`.
- Add a short docstring in the style of the neighbouring functions noting the lowercase normalisation.
out_of_scope: Changes to orders, payments, or any HTTP/API layer

tasks.title: Add get and update primitives to Database
tasks.description:
In `shop/db.py`, extend the in-memory `Database` class with two small methods that the users service (and any other caller) can use independently:

- `get(self, table: str, row_id: int) -> dict | None` — return the row with the given id, implemented by delegating to the existing `find_one(table, id=row_id)` so the scan logic is not duplicated.
- `update(self, table: str, row_id: int, values: dict) -> bool` — look the row up by id (reuse `get`/`find_one`), and if found merge `values` into the existing dict in place so the row stored in `self.tables` is mutated. Return `True` when a row was updated and `False` when no row with that id exists. The `id` key must never be overwritten: strip/ignore any `id` entry present in `values`.

Keep the style consistent with the existing methods (type hints, no external deps, no docstring-heavy additions beyond what neighbours have).
tasks.definition_of_done: `Database.get(table, row_id)` returns the matching row dict or `None`, and is implemented via `find_one(table, id=row_id)`. `Database.update(table, row_id, values)` mutates the existing row dict in place (visible through `self.tables` and previously-obtained references), returns `True` on success and `False` for an unknown id, and leaves `row['id']` unchanged even if `values` contains an `id` key. Both methods work for any table without depending on the users module.

tasks.title: Add EmailTaken exception and change_email service
tasks.description:
In `shop/users.py`, add email-change support following the existing service conventions (`Database` as the first argument, lowercase email normalisation):

- Define `class EmailTaken(Exception): pass` directly alongside the existing `UserNotFound` exception.
- Add `change_email(db: Database, user_id: int, new_email: str) -> User` with a short docstring in the style of the neighbouring functions noting that emails are normalised to lowercase.
- Implementation order matters: normalise with `new_email.lower()`; fetch the current row via `db.get("users", user_id)` and raise `UserNotFound(user_id)` if it is `None`; then call `db.find_one("users", email=normalised)` and raise `EmailTaken(normalised)` only if a row is found whose `id` differs from `user_id` (re-setting one's own email is a no-op success); then call `db.update("users", user_id, {"email": normalised})` and return `User(row["id"], normalised, row["password_hash"])`.

Do not touch orders, payments, or any HTTP/API layer.
tasks.definition_of_done: `shop/users.py` exports `EmailTaken` next to `UserNotFound` and a `change_email(db, user_id, new_email)` that: returns a `User` with the lowercased email and the row's existing `password_hash` after persisting the change through `db.update`; raises `UserNotFound(user_id)` for an unknown id even when the target email is already taken; raises `EmailTaken(normalised)` when another user already owns the email; and succeeds without error when the email already belongs to the same `user_id`. Subsequent `get_user_by_email(db, new_email)` finds the user.

spec.title: Add change_email to shop.users (plus Database update support)
spec.goal: Users currently have no way to change their email address after registration. Add a `change_email(db, user_id, new_email)` service function in `shop/users.py` that normalises the new email to lowercase, rejects emails already taken by another user, and fails cleanly for unknown user ids. The in-memory `Database` needs a lookup-by-id and a row update primitive to support this.
constraints: Reuse existing exception types where they already exist (`UserNotFound`); new exceptions live alongside it in `shop/users.py`
acceptance_criteria: `Database` gains the methods needed to look a row up by id and to update fields on an existing row, usable independently of the users module
spec.technical_notes:
In `shop/db.py`, add two small methods to `Database`:
- `get(table, row_id) -> dict | None` — implement via the existing `find_one(table, id=row_id)` to avoid duplicating the scan logic.
- `update(table, row_id, values) -> bool` — locate the row by id and merge `values` into it in place (mutating the dict already in `self.tables`), returning whether a row was updated. Never allow `id` to be overwritten.

In `shop/users.py`:
- Add `class EmailTaken(Exception): pass` next to `UserNotFound`.
- `change_email(db, user_id, new_email)`: normalise with `new_email.lower()`; fetch the current row with `db.get("users", user_id)` and raise `UserNotFound(user_id)` if it is `None`; check for a conflict with `db.find_one("users", email=normalised)` and raise `EmailTaken(normalised)` only if the found row's `id` differs from `user_id`; then `db.update("users", user_id, {"email": normalised})` and return `User(row["id"], normalised, row["password_hash"])`.
- Order matters: unknown-id check before the taken-email check, so a bogus id with a taken email raises `UserNotFound`.
- Add a short docstring in the style of the neighbouring functions noting the lowercase normalisation.
out_of_scope: Changes to orders, payments, or any HTTP/API layer
